title: Recall SQL Pattern Playbook
note: Original expansion of the site's 14-pattern summary; starter SQL examples use PostgreSQL-style features.

cards.name: Window ranking
cards.cue: Rank people, products, or scores inside each group.
cards.memory: WINDOW ranks rows without collapsing them.
cards.watch: RANK skips numbers after ties; DENSE_RANK does not.
cards.recall: Which rank keeps equal scores tied?

cards.name: Top N by group
cards.cue: Find the best 3 or newest 5 within EACH group.
cards.memory: PARTITION resets the ranking for every group.
code: PARTITION BY team ORDER BY score DESC
cards.watch: Use DENSE_RANK to include all ties at the cutoff.
cards.recall: Why not use LIMIT 3 for top 3 per team?

cards.name: Running totals
cards.cue: Show the total SO FAR for every date or transaction.
cards.memory: SUM OVER + ORDER BY = rolling accumulation.
cards.watch: Choose a stable order and explicit ROWS frame.
cards.recall: What changes with PARTITION BY user_id?

cards.name: Previous / next
cards.cue: Compare an event with the event immediately before or after.
cards.memory: LAG looks BACK; LEAD looks AHEAD.
cards.watch: Sort deterministically; first row has no prior row.
cards.recall: Which function compares today with yesterday?

cards.name: Self joins
cards.cue: One row refers to another row in the SAME table.
cards.memory: One table, two roles, two aliases.
cards.watch: LEFT JOIN retains workers without a manager.

cards.name: Anti-joins
cards.cue: Find customers with NO orders or items with NO matches.
cards.memory: NOT EXISTS means prove the match is absent.
cards.watch: NOT IN is unsafe if its subquery returns NULL.
cards.recall: Which clause finds customers who never ordered?

cards.name: Grouped aggregates
cards.cue: One answer per city, department, or product category.
cards.memory: GROUP BY changes the GRAIN of the output.
cards.watch: WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters groups.
cards.recall: Where do you filter groups with 3+ orders?

cards.name: Conditional pivots
cards.cue: Show categories side by side as separate output columns.
cards.memory: CASE chooses a bucket; SUM adds that bucket.
code: THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS a_sales,
THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS b_sales
cards.watch: Check NULLs, the ELSE branch, and row grain.
cards.recall: What creates separate A and B columns?

cards.name: Deduplication
cards.cue: Keep the latest or preferred row for each ID.
cards.memory: Rank within each ID, then KEEP row one.
code: ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC
cards.watch: Add a tie-breaker: updated_at may not be unique.

cards.name: CTE pipelines
cards.cue: Turn a messy problem into named, smaller query steps.
cards.memory: WITH is a notebook of intermediate answers.
cards.watch: CTEs improve readability, not always runtime.
cards.recall: When are multiple named CTE steps useful?

cards.name: Correlated subqueries
cards.cue: For each outer row, test a related condition.
cards.memory: The inner query refers BACK to an outer row.
cards.watch: EXISTS checks existence; inspect plan for speed.
cards.recall: Which outer alias does the inner query use?

cards.name: Gaps and islands
cards.cue: Find streaks of consecutive dates, IDs, or numbers.
cards.memory: For consecutive ints: value minus row_num = island.
code: FROM (SELECT DISTINCT value FROM nums) d
cards.watch: Deduplicate first; date math varies by SQL dialect.
cards.recall: Why does the subtraction find a streak?

cards.name: Date cohorts
cards.cue: Group users by first activity; follow later behavior.
cards.memory: FIRST event = cohort; LATER event = activity.
cards.watch: This query counts cohort sizes, not retention.

cards.name: Recursive queries
cards.cue: Walk an org chart or parent-child hierarchy.
cards.memory: ANCHOR starts; RECURSION follows; STOP guards.
code: FROM employees e JOIN org o
cards.watch: Depth limits help; visited IDs also prevent cycles.
cards.recall: Identify the anchor and recursive parts.

quiz: Latest status row for each user?
Orders per region, only regions with 5+?
Monthly new users by signup month?
Apple and banana sales in separate columns?
Find every descendant of a category?
Make a query readable in 3 stages?
Give each student's rank inside the class?
